threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You stop at the traffic lights and look confused when cyclists breeze past without a care in the world—welcome to London Fields!
Heard a guy on the 3 bus brag about his 'late-night curry strike'—claiming he’s tried every place open after midnight. Must be a Brixton rite of passage.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of currywurst wafting from the Imbiss on Sonnenallee, mixed with the sound of a street artist's guitar, hit different one rainy Sunday afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a club that turns into a pancake house by day, with DJs spinning tunes while you feast on brunch.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name at least three taco trucks that aren’t La Taqueria or El Farolito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a sequined suit doing the moonwalk in front of a Muni stop while waiting for the 47—only in SF can a bus delay turn into a dance party.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always mistake the 'ku' in 'Kiosk' for a trendy café; it’s just where they sell lottery tickets and newspapers. Such a simple, local spot.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled at the menu prices in the local bodega; everyone else just knows to ask for the 'menú del dia' right away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for the bus instead of nudging your way in. Locals just seem to merge into the crowd like clockwork.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham and the driver sang along to every song on the radio. Had me chuckling all the way home.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The night I heard a group of kids rapping outside, one of them freestyling about the weeds in the park. It felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg street artists tag not just walls but also bus stops? It's like a gallery for the everyday commute.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows not to trust BART on a Friday evening—those overheated brakes are a telltale sign. Tourists just scramble for an Uber.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy confidently strutting off a packed bus with a full pizza in hand, just before it lurched and sent two people tumbling. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for lounging, but locals actually use them for quick chats and impromptu music sessions. It's a vibe you miss.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look at the TMB map like it’s a treasure map, lost in their own adventure while the locals glide by.
